title.narrative: Promoting Gender-Sensitive, Resilient, Affordable and Adequate Housing for Internal Displaced People in Cabo Delgado Province

description.narrative: Conflicts and climate shocks experienced since 2017 caused by climate change, particularly the intermittency between droughts and floods and, more recently, the cyclical cyclones that affect the Centre and North regions in particular, destroy infrastructures, take away sources of income and survival and place women and men in internally displaced people, dependent on support and living in degrading conditions. The same situation is being created by the conflict led by extremists in Cabo Delgado. The massive pressure of displaced persons risks to people's survival, especially for women and children, who make up the majority. For women and girls, the risks are associated with the lack of housing and land property, and limited access to sexual and reproductive health services and care. In addition, due to the lack of alternatives girls and women or their families tends to adopt negative coping mechanisms that include sex work and early unions. As displaced, women and girls are also exposed to physical violence and sexual exploitation and abuse. Housing has proved to be one of the primary needs to ensure a proper resettlement of displaced families in these contexts. Among the IDPs, there are mostly young women and girls, who together with children and the older persons constitute a vulnerable group and need special attention. They are the ones who most often suffer from traumas caused by displacement and resettlement, and many of them need support through protection mechanisms that allow them to reduce their vulnerability in the face of gender violence, discrimination and marginalization. There have been cases of women abuses in the process of displacement and allocation of plots, housing, access to basic services and health care, where particular attention and advocacy is also needed from the point of view of the spatial definition of new settlements. Possible housing solutions should be diversified according to the location, and have as influencing factors the culture, customs, the availability of local construction materials and the financial capacity for construction and maintenance. Therefore, the housing models and shelters that are often implemented in humanitarian crises of this type have not responded, in a way, to ensure adequate conditions of security, resilience, provision of basic services, safe and suitable places for cooking (especially in times of heavy rainfall) and security of adequate land and property ownership. However, the criteria for dimensioning and designing housing models must take into account the needs of this target group, defined through inclusive participatory planning dynamics, where women and girls can be heard and actively involved in the process. In consideration of these aspects raised above and associated with several other contexts,in 2019, after Mozambique was strongly hit by Cyclones Idai in Sofala Province and Kenneth in Cabo Delgado Province, UN-Habitat Mozambique Country Office developed Building Back Better and Resilience Building Umbrella Programme (2019-2024) with the overall objective to enhance the climate adaptation capacity of the Mozambican people and their institutions and achieve more resilient human settlements. The Umbrella Programme aims at working as a common and coherent framework that will guide UN-Habitat short, medium and long-term projects, programmes and engagements regarding the post-cyclone reconstruction and building resilience. It is being operationalized through two complementary axes of interventions to support the recovery and reconstruction process in Mozambique: Axis 1- Building Back Better Safer (BBB) Schools, Hospitals and Resilient Housing and Axis 2 - Enhancing Urban Resilience through Integrated Approaches. In addition, since the beginning of 2020 the conflict in Northern Mozambique between government forces and Non-State Armed Groups (NSAG) has been intensifying resulting in massive internal displacement of more that 1 million people until end of 2022. In 2020, UN-Habitat released a Position Paper raising the issue of the territorial dimension of displacement in Northern Mozambique and delineating the Agency’s potential role in support of planning, management and implementation of urban and rural interventions to address both humanitarian and recovery needs in Cabo Delgado. As a follow up, two years later the Mozambique Country Office developed the Multi-scale Integrated Territorial Approach Umbrella Programme for Northern Mozambique (2022 – 2026) to intervene simultaneously and coherently at different territorial scales (levels) to transform the crisis affecting Northern Mozambique into an opportunity to achieve the Humanitarian-Development-Peace Nexus.
